{"answer": "The contexts support the claim: chronic aerobic exercise alters endothelial function and improves NO-mediated vasodilating mechanisms. Studies report increased NO production/NOx, increased cGMP, enhanced bradykinin-mediated relaxation with increased ecNOS mRNA, and upregulated eNOS/iNOS expression after training.", "citations": [{"chunk_index": 0, "quote": "The present study suggests that even a mild regular aerobic-endurance exercise increases NO production in previously sedentary older humans, which may have beneficial effects (i.e., antihypertensive and antiatherosclerotic effects by endogenous NO) on the cardiovascular system."}, {"chunk_index": 2, "quote": "The present study suggests that chronic exercise causes an increase in production of NO and a decrease in production of ET-1 in humans, which may produce beneficial effects (i.e., vasodilative and antiatherosclerotic) on the cardiovascular system."}, {"chunk_index": 4, "quote": "These data indicate that exercise training enhances bradykinin-mediated relaxation of collateral-dependent LCx arterioles isolated after chronic coronary occlusion, most likely because of effects on ecNOS mRNA expression and increased production of NO."}, {"chunk_index": 1, "quote": "Our results show that chronic exercise increases both iNOS and eNOS gene expression in endothelium."}], "abstained": false}
